page.title: CV | Jingwei Cui
cv.name: Jingwei Cui
cv.headline: PhD candidate in Food Science, Jiangnan University · Joint PhD at the National University of Singapore · Graduating June 2027
sum.1: Trained in QDA, triangle tests, preference tests and sensory study design. Have recruited, screened, trained and calibrated sensory panels, and led industry-commissioned sensory evaluation and flavor screening projects, following data collection and quality-control standards for human-subject research. Decomposed the variance of individual perception and tested for consumer preference segments (none were stable in the data).
sum.2: Python, MATLAB and SQL. In perception research I have built, tuned and validated neural network, ensemble, random forest, XGBoost and Gaussian process regression models, and I use ANOVA, PCA and other multivariate methods.
sum.3: Combine instrument data (electronic nose, electronic tongue, GC-MS) with sensory panel and consumer preference data in one model. Wrote, on my own, an automated GC-MS data-processing system (3,000+ samples) and electronic-nose data extraction code (5,000+ samples) that turn raw instrument output into model-ready data. Designed and managed an analytical database.
sum.4: Operate GC-MS, GC-O, GC×GC-MS, electronic nose and electronic tongue independently. Familiar with identifying and quantifying key aroma compounds and with OAV/ROAV analysis, and with relating instrument results to sensory findings.
sum.5: 8 first-author SCI papers (5 published, 3 submitted), 2 granted invention patents, and 2 English oral presentations accepted at the IUFoST 2026 World Congress. Present results in English to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior managers.

dev.1: Designed and built 8 browser-based tools for flavor and perception research: odor and taste prediction from molecular structure; an odor-space map of 5,000 aroma molecules; ingredient and substitute search from a flavor brief; GC-MS peak-table parsing with OAV/ROAV ranking of key aroma compounds; analysis of individual perception differences (including a test for consumer segments). All computation runs locally in the browser; raw data are not uploaded.
dev.2: Designed, built and maintain a program that extracts and analyses GC-MS data after manual peak integration: automatic retention-time matching, merging of adjacent peaks, and rule-based choice of the flavor compound when one peak has several library candidates. Cut secondary data processing from hours to minutes and removed manual transcription errors; in routine research use, 3,000+ samples so far.
dev.3: Extracts data from raw txt files and performs baseline correction and resistance calculation, replacing manual per-sample processing; 5,000+ electronic-nose samples processed, giving standardized input for modeling.
ind.1.h: A restaurant chain, Sensory Evaluation Lead
ind.1.1: Designed and executed the sensory evaluation protocol, carrying out systematic flavor screening across multiple prototype samples.
ind.1.2: Cross-validated instrumental flavor profiling with sensory evaluation to set up a repeatable evaluation procedure.
ind.2.proj: Aroma profiling and flavor evaluation of coffee beans
ind.2.1: Applied GC-O-MS and ROAV to characterize coffee-bean aroma and established a systematic flavor-profiling and evaluation method.
ind.2.2: Built an actionable flavor-screening and evaluation workflow, used in product flavor development.
ind.3.h: A multinational dairy / infant-nutrition company, Core Contributor
ind.3.proj: Compositional analysis and lipid database construction
ind.3.1: Established a standardized sample-preparation and GC quantification workflow and measured fatty acids in large batches of milk samples.
ind.3.2: Led the design and curation of a lipid database, organized for reuse.
ind.4.proj: Quality control and oxidative stability of frying oil
ind.4.1: Handled oil quality control and oxidative-stability evaluation, measuring acid value, peroxide value and oxidative stability index among other indicators.
ind.4.2: Built a kinetic method for characterizing oil oxidative degradation, used for shelf-life assessment.
res.1.h: Ph.D. thesis: Recognition, prediction and simulation of human milk flavor using end-to-end neural networks based on electronic nose data
res.1.1: Classification model: discriminates human milk, several mammalian milks and infant formula from electronic nose resistance data.
res.1.2: Prediction model: ensemble learning framework predicting key flavor-active compounds directly from electronic nose response features.
res.1.3: Weight model: quantified the contribution of maternal mood, diet, and milk fatty acid / amino acid composition to human milk flavor.
res.1.4: Optimization model: optimized fatty acid and amino acid types and ratios in infant formula to bring formula flavor closer to human milk.
res.2.h: Master's thesis: Neural network prediction of beef flavor compounds from hydrolysis–Maillard reaction of beef tallow residue
res.2.1: Flavor prediction model accounting for interactions between volatile compounds to predict overall sample flavor.
res.2.2: Curve-fitting model for ROAV of volatile compounds as a function of enzymatic hydrolysis time.
res.2.3: Additive optimization model selecting the optimal ratio among 17 amino acids, balancing flavor against cost.
sk.1: QDA, triangle tests, preference tests and other sensory methodologies; panel recruitment, screening, training and calibration; sensory experimental design and controlled testing environments; collection, curation and statistical analysis of sensory and consumer data.
sk.2: Python, MATLAB, SQL; ANOVA, PCA and other multivariate methods; neural networks, SVM, random forest, XGBoost, Gaussian process regression, K-means clustering; grid search, ensembling and regularization; particle swarm and Bayesian optimization.
sk.3: Visual Studio; Python automation scripts and browser-based tool development; ECharts; MS Office; technical writing and presentation slides.
sk.4: Electronic nose, electronic tongue, GC, GC-O, GC-MS, GC×GC-MS; HS-SPME sample preparation; OAV / ROAV characterization of key aroma compounds; fatty acid and amino acid quantification.
